newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee gains on dollar sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee gains on dollar sell-off.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was higher in early Wednesday trade, as banks continued to sell dollars on indications that the central bank was comfortable with the current exchange rate, dealers said.
At 0430 GMT the rupee was at 58.72, after opening at 58.68 and climbing to 58.60 when the central bank pushed down the dollar, they said. The rupee closed at 58.80 to the dollar on Tuesday.
The central bank pushed down the dollar by three-quarter local cent, fixing buying and selling at 58.2095 and 59.3855.

"There was no trading until the central bank announced its intentions," said a Seylan Bank dealer. "After which there was heavy selling which brought the dollar down to 58.60 when there was some buy-back."
Banks which have been holding on to dollars due to a lack of imports and the central bank's recent bullishness towards the greenback, were unwinding positions, he said.
"Banks believe the central bank's action on Tuesday and Wednesday shows that short-term dollar-rupee exchange rate targets have been met," said a foreign bank dealer.
On Tuesday the central bank left the exchange rate unchanged depsite overseas gains by the greenback.
Overnight call money, meanwhile remained between at around 10.5 percent, dealers said.
